text: In the Jordan canonical form of an operator T, the number of Jordan blocks with eigenvalue λ equals:
choices: dim ker(T − λI), the geometric multiplicity
the multiplicity of λ as a root of the minimal polynomial
the size of the largest block for λ
explanation: Each Jordan block J_k(λ) contributes exactly one independent eigenvector, so blocks are counted by dim E_λ. The algebraic multiplicity is the SUM of the block sizes for λ, and the multiplicity of λ in the minimal polynomial is the size of the LARGEST block.
